sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ for the death of Sri. Naveen Kumar H.S. S/o Srinivasa in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 15.06.2022 at about 6.45 a.m., when the husband of the Petitioner No.1 by name Naveen Kumar was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA08U 9543 on NH75 Bengaluru - Mangalore road, near Chakenahalli, in front of Bhairaweshwara Hotel, Yadeyur Hobli, Tumkur District, at that time, driver of the Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019 was parked his vehicle on the road with negligent manner, without any indicator and signals like reflector and without putting any barricades and even without keeping any person to give signals at the spot.
Due to unable to ascertain about SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4057/2022 parking of the vehicle, said Naveen Kumar's motorcycle was dashed to said Milk tanker from back side.
Due to the impact, Naveen Kumar had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body and died on the spot.
Thereafter, Post mortem was conducted at Government hospital, Kunigal and body was handed over to the Petitioners.
The Petitioners had spent about Rs.2,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.

Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Security Guard at M/s Security and Intelligence Service India Ltd.,
Rajalakshmi T vs Hanumantharayappa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58938946/
2 Kunigal and Milk Vendor and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Naveen Kumar, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4057/2022 compensation to the Petitioners.

3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statements to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the deceased.

Further he contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was parked the vehicle on the left side of the road and the driver had valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
Further he contended that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the Respondent No.2.
Hence, he is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, on these grounds the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against him.

SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4057/2022 The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased and also the accident caused by the negligent parking by the driver of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Naveen Kumar due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.

Further it contended that as on the alleged date of the accident the driver of the milk tanker has parked the vehicle on the correct side of the road as per the traffic rules and regulations by putting parking lights on and he has taken all the precautionary measures and there was no negligence on his part.
It is obligatory on the part of the deceased to take all care to avoid the accident, but the deceased failed to do so.
The alleged accident was caused due to carelessness of the deceased himself.

Further it contended that as per records it is very clear that there was much space for the deceased to move his vehicle, but he rode his vehicle unmindfully and negligently and he himself caused the accident.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4057/2022 to dismiss the Petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Naveen Kumar S/o Srinivasa was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.06.2022 at about 6.45 a.m., near Chakenahalli, in front of Bhairaweshwara hotel, Yadeyur hobli, Tumkur, due to the negligent parking of the Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019 on the public road, without putting indicator and without taking precaution?

3 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Naveen Kumar?

On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
The Respondent No.1 did not choose to lead evidence.

6. Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4057/2022 Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :

9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and reiterated the averments made in the petition.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, PW1 has SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4057/2022 relied on Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

Ex.P1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that the Amruthur Police have registered the case against the driver of Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06 AA9019 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

and 4 are the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.5 is the Inquest mahazar.

Ex.P7 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P8 is the true copy of the ChargeSheet which shows that the Amruthur Police has Rajalakshmi T vs Hanumantharayappa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58938946/

PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for Respondent No.2.

But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
12.

The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending Milk Tanker for negligent parking of the offending vehicle and causing the accident and due to the said accident, the husband of the PW1 had succumbed to the injuries.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its officer by name Chandana C.S and got marked Authorization letter, Copy of Policy, Copy of Notice and Postal Receipt at Ex.R1 to 4.
In the crossexamination she admitted that she does not had personal knowledge about the accident.

The Chargesheet contents shows that on the alleged date, the driver of the offending vehicle negligently parked his vehicle on the road without putting indicator and at that time the deceased by SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4057/2022 riding his motorcycle came on the said road and since one lorry and one car was proceeding by his right side and there was no place to him to move further, his motorcycle dashed to the backside of the lorry and thereby accident occurred and he sustained injuries and he succumbed to the injuries.

It is to be worth to note here that the Respondent No.1 who is the owner of the vehicle has not whispered that the driver has challenged the Chargesheet filed against him or he tried to lodge Complaint.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Milk Tanker and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "in the Affirmative."

13. Issue No.2 and 3: All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4057/2022 and to avoid repetition of facts.
14.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the mother and father of the deceased Naveen Kumar.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of Petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.9 to P.12.
Ex.P13 is the Marriage Invitation card of the Petitioner No.1 with Naveen Kumar.
Hence, the said documents shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Naveen Kumar,
they entitled for the compensation.

15. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 22 years and deceased was working as a Security Guard at M/s Security and Intelligence Service India Pvt. Ltd., Kunigal and was doing Milk business and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.

16. Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Naveen Kumar as 22 years at the time of the accident.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.12 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Naveen Kumar which shows his date of birth as 13.03.1993.
The alleged accident was occurred on 15.06.2022.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Naveen Kumar SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4057/2022 was 29 years, 3 months and 2 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Naveen Kumar to be taken at 30 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind his wife and parents.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the mother and father and they are considered as dependents on the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4057/2022 Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case,
since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/ to Rs.48,400/. Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/ each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the wife, mother and father of the deceased Naveen Kumar, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/ each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/ towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/ towards funeral expenses.

20.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and support in her young age and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are the mother and father of deceased Naveen Kumar, who lost son's love Rajalakshmi T vs Hanumantharayappa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58938946/
6 and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
21. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

23.

15,500/ comes to Rs.6,200/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,700/ p.m. (Rs.15,500/ + Rs.6,200/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 17.

After deducting 1/3rd towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,700/, it comes to Rs.14,467/ (Rs.21,700/  7,233/) and multiplier applied is 17 which comes to Rs.29,51,268/ (14,467 x 12 x 17).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,51,268/ towards loss of dependency.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4057/2022 compensation of Rs.31,87,768/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,87,768/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4057/2022 amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out SCCH 15 25 MVC No.4057/2022 of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 and 3, 75% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 respectively by way of Epayment and after their proper identification and the remaining 25% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ for the death of Sri. Naveen Kumar H.S. S/o Srinivasa in a Road Traffic accident.
Due to the impact, Naveen Kumar had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body and died on the spot.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Naveen Kumar, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4057/2022 compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and filed their Objection statements to the main Petition.
The Respondent No.1 in his Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the deceased.
Further he contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was parked the vehicle on the left side of the road and the driver had valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
Further he contended that the offending vehicle was duly insured with the Respondent No.2.
Hence, he is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Further it contended that as on the alleged date of the accident the driver of the milk tanker has parked the vehicle on the correct side of the road as per the traffic rules and regulations by putting parking lights on and he has taken all the precautionary measures and there was no negligence on his part.
The alleged accident was caused due to carelessness of the deceased himself.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Naveen Kumar S/o Srinivasa was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 15.06.2022 at about 6.45 a.m., near Chakenahalli, in front of Bhairaweshwara hotel, Yadeyur hobli, Tumkur, due to the negligent parking of the Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019 on the public road, without putting indicator and without taking precaution?
Rajalakshmi T vs Hanumantharayappa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58938946/
3 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Naveen Kumar?
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4057/2022 3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?
5.
REASONS 7. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that Naveen Kumar was died in the accident that occurred due to negligent parking of the offending Milk Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA06AA9019 by its driver.
8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending Milk Tanker for negligent parking of the offending vehicle and causing the accident and due to the said accident, the husband of the PW1 had succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Milk Tanker and in the said accident, the husband of PW.1 was succumbed to the injuries.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,51,268/ towards loss of dependency.
25. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,45,200/
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/ of dead body 6.
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of SCCH 15 22 MVC No.4057/2022 Rs.31,87,768/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for SCCH 15 23 MVC No.4057/2022 compensation of Rs.31,87,768/ along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,87,768/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award SCCH 15 24 MVC No.4057/2022 amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of Epayment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out SCCH 15 25 MVC No.4057/2022 of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 and 3, 75% each of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 respectively by way of Epayment and after their proper identification and the remaining 25% each of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in respectively in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of their choice.
